Recovery & Condition Programs

Post-Surgical Recovery

Everyone prefers recovering from surgery in their own bed, but the first couple of weeks take careful attention. Our nurses and therapists come to your home to care for your incision, help manage pain and blood thinners, and get you moving safely under your surgeon's orders.

Call (818) 630-5702Request care
Provided by
Registered nurses and your Royal care team
Ordered by
Your physician or allowed practitioner
Availability
Mon to Fri, 9:00 AM to 5:30 PM, with a nurse on call after hours
Where
In your home, across 4 Southern California counties

Overview

About Post-Surgical Recovery

After an operation, our registered nurses inspect and dress your incision, watch for early signs of infection or blood clots, and help you stay on top of your pain and medication schedule. If your surgeon has you on injectable blood thinners or surgical drains, we take care of those and show your family how to manage them safely.

Getting moving again is just as important as resting. When your surgeon orders rehabilitation, physical and occupational therapists work with you right in your own hallway, bedroom, and bathroom so you can climb steps, shower, and move around your home with confidence.

What's included

  • Surgical incision checks, sterile dressing changes, and staple or suture care
  • Pain management support and safe medication scheduling
  • Close monitoring for infection, swelling, or blood clots (DVT)
  • Blood thinner education and injections when prescribed
  • Surgical drain measurement and care when ordered
  • In-home physical and occupational therapy coordinated by Royal
  • Training on safe bed transfers, walkers, and stair safety
  • Direct progress updates sent to your surgeon and primary doctor

Who it helps

  • Patients coming home after hip, knee, or shoulder replacement
  • People recovering from back, spine, abdominal, or general surgery
  • Patients healing after heart or vascular procedures
  • Individuals recovering after an amputation, including mobility and prosthetic training

What to expect

Your care, step by step.

  1. 01

    Step 1: Referral & orders

    Your doctor sends orders over, or you give us a call and we reach out to your doctor's office for you.

  2. 02

    Step 2: Nurse assessment

    One of our registered nurses visits you at home, listens to how you are doing, and goes over your medical needs.

  3. 03

    Step 3: Your plan of care

    We partner with your doctor to map out the right services, visit schedule, and recovery goals for you.

  4. 04

    Step 4: Care & coordination

    Your team visits on schedule, shows your family how to help, and keeps your doctor in the loop as you get stronger.

Staying safe

When to call us or your doctor

Our office is open Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 5:30 PM. A registered nurse is always on call by phone after office hours, on weekends, and on holidays.

Call us or your physician if you notice:

  • Increasing redness, warmth, swelling, or thick drainage at the incision
  • A fever above the temperature threshold in your discharge paperwork
  • New calf tenderness, warmth, or swelling in one leg
  • Pain that stays severe even after taking your prescribed medicine

For chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of stroke, severe bleeding or any emergency, call 911.

Questions

Post-Surgical Recovery FAQs

All frequently asked questions

Will I get physical therapy at home after joint replacement?

Yes, whenever your surgeon orders it. We coordinate licensed physical and occupational therapists who come directly to your house, so your rehabilitation and nursing visits work together under one plan.

How long does home health care last after surgery?

It depends on the procedure and how quickly you heal. Many surgical patients need home visits for a few weeks until they can comfortably travel to outpatient therapy or their surgeon's office.

Do I qualify as homebound right after surgery?

After major surgery, most patients find that leaving the house takes a taxing physical effort or requires a walker and another person's help. For that recovery period, you are usually considered homebound. Give us a call and we will talk it through with you.
